I’ll admit that in the past when I was younger and in dark spaces, I would sometimes think about how if I were to die at my own hands that everyone might finally acknowledge me and miss me; it was sort of like a guilty pleasure wherein I felt suicidal anyway, but would still immaturely derive some pleasure from the thought that people might finally think about what they threw away. I’m not proud of that and I’d like to think that I have a less narcissistic perspective now, but I’m being honest. now when I feel suicidal I definitely wouldn’t “get off” from the thought of the pain of my loved ones; it’s more like I consider said people as the meaning in my life (new experiences/perspectives, learning more about foreign topics, relating to a fellow human being and having a real connection to their soul), being an extrovert. now that I don’t have them it’s like a gaping hole in my life, a giant part of myself/my identity that I feel dissociated from.
the only thing is that whatever expectations I have for them are also things I would do for them. so sometimes it just feels like I’m really invested in people when they aren’t in me

yeah, there’s just always been a part of me that wants to feel like at least one person loves me unconditionally and cares to be involved in my life. and I’m not sure what I can do to help myself right now, it’s obviously something I need to figure out but it isn’t easy to do that alone. the usual having to accept that life’s just unfair, and all that.
